CANONICAL_NAME.value: Whitaker's Words -- a Latin morphological analyser and dictionary in Ada (Col. William Whitaker, 1993-2006; maintained by Martin Keegan)

VERSION.value: github.com/mk270/whitakers-words master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: A large REAL Ada program (tens of thousands of lines) from the language's first generation: parses Latin word forms into stem + inflection against a 39,000-entry dictionary, handling enclitics, tackons, prefixes/suffixes and syncope; runs on DOS/Windows/Unix for three decades. Public domain by its author. The Ada culture's strong typing and packages are visible throughout.

value.built_to: explain any Latin word form by finding which stem plus which inflection could produce it, against a real dictionary
value.pressure: morphological ambiguity, a large dictionary, DOS-era memory limits the design still shows
value.success_means: known forms parse to the right lemma and inflection; unknown forms are reported as such

value.pressure: ambiguity, dictionary scale, limited memory (1990s PCs)
value.failure_condition: a form is parsed to a wrong lemma or missed

cut.note: analysis by generate-and-test over the word's suffixes: every ending of length Z that matches the word's tail proposes a (stem, inflection) pair; the stems are looked up in a dictionary indexed by first letters; a surviving pair must agree between the inflection's part/declension/key and the dictionary entry's; failures fall through a fixed ladder of repairs (syncope, enclitics, prefixes, suffixes, orthographic 'tricks') each of which re-runs the same core

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: Run_Inflections (205-305): Lelf/Lell index by (Z, last letter); the blank-ending pass; Sa(stem_length)
organs.mechanism: the inflection table is read in one of four sections chosen by the word's last letter; for each ending length Z from the maximum down to 1, the endings indexed by (Z, last letter) are compared with the word's last Z characters; each match yields a parse record (stem = word minus Z, the inflection record) and marks stem length Z as possible; the blank ending is always added first for words within the stem-size limit
organs.output: a list of (stem, inflection) candidates and the set of possible stem lengths
assumptions: Latin inflection is suffixal (prefixes are handled separately as 'fixes'); the table indexed by (length, last letter) makes the trial cheap
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: every morphologically possible split is enumerated without a grammar
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: no ranking here; the ambiguity is resolved later by dictionary agreement and a sort
organs.human_prior: finite-state morphology (Koskenniemi 1983) is the contemporaneous alternative; Whitaker's is table-driven generate-and-test

organs.human_name: Reduce_Stem_List (736-870): the three '<=' agreement operators; the suffix/prefix root and target checks
organs.mechanism: for each reduced-dictionary entry (PDL) and each candidate: if a suffix is in play the entry's part must be compatible with the suffix's root part and key, and the entry is transformed to the suffix's target part; a prefix must match the (possibly transformed) part or be universal; then the candidate's inflection must agree with the entry under partial-order operators: part (Pack <= Pron; X matches all), gender (C matches non-neuter; X all), stem key (0 matches all); survivors carry the dictionary entry's MNPC id
assumptions: morphological agreement is a lattice with wildcards (X, C, key 0), not equality; affixes change the entry's category before agreement
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one agreement pass filters the generate-and-test explosion; wildcards let the dictionary be underspecified
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the operators are hand-written per field; a new category means a new operator

organs.human_name: Pass (parse.adb 642-695): Roman numerals -> Word -> Try_Slury -> Perform_Syncope -> Enclitic -> (fixes on) Word -> Syncope -> Enclitic; Prune_Stems (1298-1378): Search_Dictionaries -> Apply_Prefix -> Apply_Suffix -> Apply_Prefix; Syncope (tricks.adb): -avi- -> -a-, -ivi- -> -i-, -sis/-xis-, each 'Exit loop here if SYNCOPE found hit'
organs.mechanism: the plain analysis runs first with prefix/suffix fixes disabled; if it yields nothing, a sequence of rewrites of the input word (syncopated perfects, enclitic stripping -que/-ne/-ve, orthographic flips) each re-run the same Word core and stop at the first hit, restoring Pa_Last on failure; only then are prefixes and suffixes enabled and the core re-run; the order encodes the author's judgment of prior probability ('There may be a valid simple parse, if so it is most probable')
organs.output: the first non-empty parse set along the ladder
organs.state: Pa_Last (the parse array's high-water mark) as the success signal
assumptions: earlier rungs are more probable readings than later ones; a hit at any rung ends the search (no scoring across rungs)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: rare phenomena are handled without contaminating the common case; the core is reused rather than generalised
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a word with a rare true reading and a spurious common one returns the spurious one; the author's comments say as much ('This sort is very sloppy', 'the following condition is absurd')
organs.human_prior: backoff by ordered rewrites (as in early spell correction)

rejected_cuts.candidate: Order_Stems (610-687): a bubble sort of 1-5 records by MNPC, ending size, quality, dictionary kind
rejected_cuts.note: a preference order, not a mechanism; the author calls it 'very sloppy'

rejected_cuts.candidate: Dictionary_Search / Load_Pdl (320-505): the first-two-letters index into DICTLINE
rejected_cuts.note: the index is the run-time cost centre

rejected_cuts.candidate: Apply_Prefix / Apply_Suffix bodies, Try_Tackons, Process_Packons, Process_Qu_Pronouns, the enclitic tables, the English-to-Latin side, list_package (output), the data files

rejected_cuts.evidence: enumeration, agreement and the repair ladder are three separable steps; the data files are a fourth thing

pressures.condition: an organism receives a word form; a lexicon of stems and a table of endings exist; the true analysis is one of many string-compatible splits; a small fraction of words need rewrites (syncope, enclitics, affixes)
pressures.resource_or_constraint: lexicon lookups per word; a fixed table
pressures.failure_condition: the true analysis missing from the output, or the output dominated by spurious splits
pressures.world_punishes: accepting every split; running every repair on every word (spurious hits)
pressures.world_rewards: agreement filtering with wildcards; ordered backoff
pressures.observable_consequence: precision and recall of analyses against a hand-tagged corpus (the body ships expected outputs for the Aeneid: test/10_aeneid/expected.txt) with the repair ladder enabled, disabled and reordered
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the gold split must reach 100 percent; the ladder reordered (fixes first) must lower precision on the corpus; the ladder disabled must lower recall: the world must show the two failures in opposite directions

ancestry_edges.to: Whitaker's own design (1993-); the Ada 2012 port and test corpus by the mk270 maintainers
ancestry_edges.note: from the README and the record

unexplained: dictionary indexing, affix application, tackons/packons, enclitics and the English side unread
the data files (the lexicon) are half the program and unread
residue.note: the three control mechanisms of the analyser are located; the test corpus is an oracle a Stage C run could use once an Ada compiler exists
